minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved a combined pump-station and generator RFP and revised the FY24 budget; El Forno's use change approved.
minutes.summary: The commission approved El Forno's expansion of use pending the plumbing inspector's sign-off, then spent a long stretch editing a combined RFP for pump station and generator maintenance and approved it subject to chair and vice chair review. It also voted to adopt a revised FY24 budget, heard early capital planning and rate discussion, and deferred the rest of budget and capital planning to the next meeting.

Paula proposed a one-time fee when a property adds bedrooms, as Leominster does, and will consult town counsel before a vote.
Members discussed capping billable remote alarm callouts outside business hours, settling on a monthly cap in hours.
Markup on parts kept at a set percentage after brief debate; rental equipment at cost plus markup with quotes.
Allowable purchases without DPW director pre-authorization left at the current level.
Leominster wants to raise the per-dwelling connection charge and address the rate structure.
Fitchburg's expected rate increase and retiree benefits required shifting money out of capital expenditures; draw on retained earnings is unchanged.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to adopt a revised FY24 budget, with money shifted out of capital spending toward Fitchburg usage and fringe benefits.
The commission approved a combined RFP for pump station and generator maintenance, to be sent out after review by the chair and vice chair.
The commission approved a use change at El Forno's on Electric Ave, pending sign-off from the plumbing inspector.
A vote on a one-time expansion fee for added bedrooms was put off until the town counsel consultation.
Capital planning and rate increases were deferred to the next meeting after early discussion of long-term generator and crane needs.

why_it_matters: Sewer user rates are set from this budget and the capital plan, so the shift toward Fitchburg usage and benefits, and the coming rate discussion, bear on future sewer bills.
A possible bedroom-addition fee would fall on property owners who expand a home, and it has not been voted.
watch_next: April 26: Paula's consultation with town counsel on the expansion fee, then a report back to the commission.
Next meeting: FY24 budget, rate increase and long-range capital planning, using the rate spreadsheet Paula is to send.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all three votes, the main transfers and most figures, and the differences are mostly misheard digits and names. The one real difference to check is the capital plan's yearly average: ours heard 120,000 a year and the town's minutes print $100K per year. Each record also has items the other lacks, such as the pre-authorization threshold in ours and the CTE invitation in the official minutes.
